title: The Frobenius square of a k_0-morphism is Cartesian
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and put
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q=\varphi_q^{-1}\in\operatorname{Aut}(k/k_0)$, the
geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
morphism of $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base], put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $f=f_0\times\operatorname{id}_k:X\to Y$,
where fibre products are as in [def-pc-fibre-product] and spectra and their induced morphisms as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let

$$
 g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):X\to X,\qquad
 g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):Y\to Y .
$$

Then:

1. $g_X$ and $g_Y$ are isomorphisms of schemes, with inverses
$\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma^{-1})$ and
$\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma^{-1})$;

2. $f\circ g_X=g_Y\circ f$;

3. the commutative square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
 X & \xrightarrow{\ g_X\ } & X\\
 f\downarrow & & \downarrow f\\
 Y & \xrightarrow{\ g_Y\ } & Y
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian: the morphism $(g_X,f):X\to X\times_{f,Y,g_Y}Y$ is an
isomorphism. This square, with the identification $(g_X,f)$, is the
*Frobenius square* of $f_0$.

In particular, for $Y_0=\Spec k_0$ one has $Y=s=\Spec k$ (via
$\Spec k_0\times_{k_0}k=\Spec k$), $g_Y=g_s=\Spec(\gamma)$, and for a
$k_0$-scheme $X_0$ with structure morphism $a_{X_0}$ the base change
$a_X:X\to s$ satisfies $a_X\circ g_X=g_s\circ a_X$, the square
$(a_X,g_X,g_s)$ being Cartesian.

source.place: Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.10)(i) and (1.1.11), pp. 151-152: the action of W(F/F_q) on X = X_0 (x) F through the factor F, id_{X_0} x F being 'l'action du Frobenius geometrique' of (1.1.14), p. 152; the Cartesian property is the one asserted without proof in the slopmaster2 definition def:weil-direct-image-object (literature/blueprint/slopmaster2/src/version/sketch/01_final_weil_conjectures.tex, lines 2405-2425: 'The Frobenius square for f_0 is Cartesian') and in def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius

proof.text: Put $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $u=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota):s\to S_0$, $\sigma=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $\rho=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma^{-1})$. By the field-level clause of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $\gamma$ and $\gamma^{-1}$ fix $\iota(k_0)$ and are inverse ring maps. The contravariant functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] therefore gives $u\sigma=u$, $u\rho=u$, and $\sigma\rho=\rho\sigma=\operatorname{id}_s$. Thus both maps may be used over $S_0$. Here and below juxtaposition denotes ordinary composition, with the rightmost map applied first.

source.place: Spec.map_id, Spec.map_comp, Scheme.Spec, lines 482-498; agent-written application to the two inverse field automorphisms

proof.text: For either $Z_0=X_0$ or $Z_0=Y_0$, write $Z=Z_0\times_{S_0}s$ with projections $\pi_Z:Z\to Z_0$ and $b_Z:Z\to s$. The induced map $g_Z$ is characterized by $\pi_Zg_Z=\pi_Z$ and $b_Zg_Z=\sigma b_Z$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Likewise define $h_Z=\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\times_{S_0}\rho$, with $\pi_Zh_Z=\pi_Z$ and $b_Zh_Z=\rho b_Z$. These maps exist because step 1 gives $u\sigma=u\rho=u$. The two projections of $g_Zh_Z$ are $\pi_Z$ and $\sigma\rho b_Z=b_Z$, and those of $h_Zg_Z$ are $\pi_Z$ and $\rho\sigma b_Z=b_Z$. Uniqueness in the same universal property makes both composites $\operatorname{id}_Z$. This proves clause 1 with precisely the displayed inverses, for both schemes.

source.place: pullback.lift, pullback.lift_fst, pullback.lift_snd and pullback.hom_ext (read in lines 125-235); pullback.map, lines 260-275; agent-written universal-property calculation

proof.text: The base-changed morphism $f$ has $\pi_Yf=f_0\pi_X$ and $b_Yf=b_X$, by the induced-morphism clause of [def-pc-fibre-product]; the hypothesis that $f_0$ is over $S_0$ is exactly the compatibility needed to induce it. The composites $fg_X$ and $g_Yf$ have the same two projections to $Y_0$ and $s$: respectively $f_0\pi_X$ and $\sigma b_X$. Uniqueness for the fibre product $Y$ gives $fg_X=g_Yf$, proving clause 2. Multiplying this equality by the inverses established in step 2 also gives $fh_X=h_Yf$: explicitly $h_Yfg_X=f$, hence $h_Yf=fh_X$.

source.place: pullback.lift, pullback.lift_fst, pullback.lift_snd and pullback.hom_ext (read in lines 125-235); pullback.map, lines 260-275; agent-written universal-property calculation

proof.text: Let $P=X\times_{f,Y,g_Y}Y$, with projections $r:P\to X$ and $t:P\to Y$, so $fr=g_Yt$. By step 3 and [def-pc-fibre-product], the map $\eta=(g_X,f):X\to P$ exists, with $r\eta=g_X$ and $t\eta=f$. Set $\theta=h_Xr:P\to X$. Then $\theta\eta=h_Xg_X=\operatorname{id}_X$. For the other composite, $r\eta\theta=g_Xh_Xr=r$ and $t\eta\theta=fh_Xr=h_Yfr=h_Yg_Yt=t$. The uniqueness clause for $P$ gives $\eta\theta=\operatorname{id}_P$. Thus the exact morphism $(g_X,f)$ specified in clause 3 is an isomorphism, with inverse $h_Xr$, proving that this square is Cartesian.

proof.text: If $Y_0=S_0$, its structure map is $\operatorname{id}_{S_0}$. The projection $b_Y:S_0\times_{S_0}s\to s$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(u,\operatorname{id}_s)$: one composite is immediately $\operatorname{id}_s$; the other has projections $ub_Y=\pi_Y$ and $b_Y$, so is the identity by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Under this particular identification $Y=s$, the equation $b_Yg_Y=\sigma b_Y$ identifies $g_Y$ with $g_s=\sigma$, and $f$ with the scalar-extended structure morphism $a_X=b_X$. Clauses 2 and 3 now give exactly $a_Xg_X=g_sa_X$ and the claimed Cartesian structure square with its specified comparison map.
